name: Glitchin
subcategory: neural disruptor — BCI signal interference toxin
manufacturer: Shelf lab synthesis — multiple independent sources; formula is widely shared
description: Glitchin is a synthetic compound that crosses the blood-brain barrier and generates sustained electromagnetic interference at the SNT-organic interface layer, scrambling BCI signal transmission and reception in a chaotic, unpredictable pattern. Affected subjects experience fragmented sensory input from their BCI feeds, loss of augmentation control, involuntary data broadcasts, inability to access BCI-stored information, and in cases of deep neural integration, seizure-like episodes of corrupted sensory experience. It does not damage the hardware — it makes the organic brain unable to interface with it coherently.
effects: Disruption of BCI signal transmission and reception
Fragmented, corrupted sensory overlay from BCI feeds
Involuntary broadcast of BCI data — privacy collapse
Inability to access BCI-stored memory, contacts, or credentials during effect
side_effects: Severe disorientation proportional to degree of BCI integration — heavily augmented subjects are debilitated
Unaugmented or lightly integrated subjects experience primarily nausea and mild visual disturbance
Repeated exposure causes SNT interface layer scarring — progressive integration degradation
During effect, biometric security systems relying on BCI authentication become inaccessible, locking subjects out of facilities, accounts, and secured areas
cultural_context: Glitchin is the great equalizer on the Shelf — where most people can't afford military-grade chrome, a cheap canister of Scrambler drops a corpo security operative as fast as it drops anyone else. It has become the Shelf's answer to augmented authority: gangs use it to neutralize security teams, protesters use it to blind surveillance-integrated enforcers, and small-time criminals use it to strip the BCI credentials of targets before robbing them. In Tier 3 and above, Glitchin exposure is treated as a serious crime because it represents a fundamental violation of the integrated self. On the Shelf, it's Tuesday.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 corporate operative finds herself still experiencing BCI fragmentation six days after a Glitchin exposure — something in her SNT layer is not recovering, and the repair cost is more than she makes in a year.
Someone has engineered a concentrated Glitchin aerosol capable of disrupting BCIs at 50-meter range — effectively a BCI area-denial weapon — and it just showed up at a Tier 4 political rally.
A Shelf kid with no BCI becomes unexpectedly valuable as a courier during a Glitchin-saturated gang war — the only person in the zone who can still think straight.
